description.narrative:
Besides the young women and men taking part in the TUI Academy, also their parents/caregivers will benefit from the project because of the personal transformation of the students as well as the expected increase in family income. The parents/caregivers are also invited to participate in sessions about important topics such as Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights. Also the wider community (community leaders, community childcare spaces, community protection networks, youth networks, private sector within the communities) will benefit from the youth economic empowerment and fewer cases of pregnancy, gender-based violence and sexual exploitation.
Hotels will benefit from qualified and motivated staff. Synergy will also be sought with Government institutions such as the Ministry of Women, the Ministry of Labor, the Ministry of Tourism, the Council of Adolescence and Children (CONANI), and the National Institute for Early Childhood Care (INAIPI), to see how the project and organizations’ mandates and activities can be of mutual benefit.
Since the start of the project in 2017, relationships with communities, INFOTEP, the private sector, youth networks and regional Government institutions were built and they will be further strengthened over the coming three years. This is important for reaching the project targets as well as ensuring sustainability of the project beyond the grant.
Direct beneficiaries:
• 150 disadvantaged youth aged 18-29 years (at least 60% young women)
Indirect beneficiaries (numbers TBD):
• Parents/caregivers
• INFOTEP teachers
• Hotel staff
• Alumni members
• Community members

Gender-transformative approach
The TUI Academy – just like all Plan International’s work – is guided by a gender-transformative approach which tackles the underlying causes of discrimination and inequality in six connected ways:
1. Understand and address how gender norms influence children and youth throughout their life course, from birth to adulthood.
2. Strengthen girls’ and young women’s agency over the decisions that affect them, and build their knowledge, confidence, skills, and access to and control over resources.
3. Work with and support boys and men, young and old, to embrace positive masculinities and promote gender equality, while also achieving meaningful results for them.
4. Consider girls, boys, young women and young men in all their diversity when identifying and responding to their needs and interests – a one-size-fits-all solution does not work.
5. Improve both the conditions (daily needs) as well as the social position (value or status) of girls and young women.
6. Ensure sustainability by fostering an enabling environment (including with policies) where all stakeholders work together to support children and youth on their journey towards gender
Other approaches are considered and thoroughly managed, such as: Human-centered approach This proposal is the result of a human-centered approach whereby the project stakeholders have given direct input for the project focus and strategies proposed. Two TUI Academy graduates took part in the 2-day proposal development workshop with Plan International staff in Santo Domingo in July 2022.
INFOTEP, private sector partners, government institutions and community leaders provided their input through a survey and focus group sessions. Acknowledging that development projects are not linear but continuously evolving and shaped by power relations and unexpected (external) circumstances, the feedback of key stakeholders will continuously be sought throughout the project cycle.

Greater involvement of communities: through workshops with important topics to support the development of young people in the Academy. To this end, training workshops are held to help them strengthen their organzation, among community leaders and families of the young people in the project. The topics covered: Prevention of domestic violence and abuse, care and positive parenting, prevention of gender violence. The importance of these awareness-raising workshops lies in raising awareness among family and community members about the different situations of violence that can occur within families and how to prevent them. They also provide the tools to manage the necessary protection and make the necessary demands to deal with such a situation.
Accompaniment: during the training and internship process, the youth receive support, mentoring and coaching from the project's technical team, which, through visits to the students' families, detects whether there are risks of gender-based violence or violence against children and youth in the household. If so, a referral is made and the appropriate follow-up is done through the competent institutions for each case, such as the Ministry of Women and CONANI. This support has ensured that the young women who have received such guidance remain in the TUI Academy program.
Life Skills Workshops: a simple but impactful change we have made is to work on HpV issues alongside technical training. This helps young people to put their studies into perspective in order to achieve better opportunities for their development, to value themselves, to see other possible options for their lives and to set goals for themselves. This desire to better themselves is increased with very concrete actions that help them to stay in the process.
Creation of youth structures and strengthening of the alumni network: these spaces for youth facilitate the development of cohesion processes among the youth of a community that are defined by their desire to learn and be trained in topics that are related to them such as Sexual and Reproductive Rights, Relationships, Adolescent Pregnancy, Gender Equity, among others. In addition to promoting the Academy as a valid option that provides them with other opportunities, the youth of the Academy coordinate with other youth in their communities to share work agendas that are of interest to them. In other words, the alumni network can take different roles besides just promoting the project, such as: - Acting as role models - One-on-one support/buddies for current students - Lobby and advocate for youth rights.

SUMMARY. In the Dominican Republic, youth, and young women in particular, are denied the chance to go to school and gain access to a decent job. Tourism and Hospitality (T&H) is an important sector with many job opportunities. The TUI Academy is created by TUI Care Foundation and Plan International to ensure 150 youths (aged 18-29, at least 60% female) at risk of Commercial Sexual Exploitation (CSE) in La Altagracia, Dominican Republic, are socially and economically empowered by June 2025. The TUI Academy offers them vocational skills training based on the demands from the T&H market, life skills training which includes communicating in English, and an internship at a resort or hotel that is owned/contracted by TUI. The project aims to ensure these youths can protect themselves from CSE and increases their opportunities for obtaining decent work in the T&H sector.

Sustainability: Program sustainability lies in the relationships that are being established with partners such as the private sector/hotels. Agreements will be signed to establish responsibilities and commitments with the hotels in terms of payment of internships and the acceptance of young people for internships, with the idea that once the (economic) benefit is realized, the hotels will continue this practice beyond the project.
Furthermore, working with the cooperatives and the training of trainers will ensure that SRHR education continues beyond the project. Peer educators, youth advocates and trained health care workers will ensure long-term progress on SRHR. The community campaigns and dialogues aim to shift societal and cultural norms, leading to reduced discrimination, coercion and gender-based violence in the long term.
We will continue to work with the communities to establish visibility of the project and that the lessons learned and success stories continue as motivators for the youth of the communities. The sustainability of the project also lies in continuing and strengthening conversations and support with public institutions such as the Ministry of Women, Ministry of Labor, Ministry of Youth, Ministry of Tourism, CONANI, and INAIPI. In the TUI Academy 3.0 these organizations and institutions are committed to continue their work and role in offering support for young victims of violence, support in job search and CV training as well as preparation for job interviews. We are also working on a collaboration with the Municipality of Yuma, so that the public transportation system can support the logistics of transportation for the students.

This is the third version of the TUI Academy, all of them have been with the National Institute of Vocational Technical Training (INFOTEP) and the BDR hotel group as its main partners since 2017.
Since then approaches to the hotel sector have been made in order to grow partnership for the project. Conversation with hotels such as Club Med, Barcelo Bavaro, Riu Hotels and Resorts, Ocean El Faro, Ocean Blue, Palladium Hotels have been part of the implementation. In the present very good relationship between TUI Project and ASOLESTE (hotel association of the East) for implementation support are in progress.

Youth unemployment and poverty in the country are high, even though hotels and resorts are looking for skilled staff. In fact, already in August 2021 the Ministry of Tourism reported that the tourism industry in the Dominican Republic had largely recovered after the COVID-19 dip and already 80.000 new jobs had been created in tourism: an increase of 104% since August 2021.
However, despite the promising job perspectives, many youths have low levels of education, and therefore lack the relevant knowledge and skills to work in the tourism sector. At the same time, adolescents and youth - especially girls and young women - face severe risks of being(sexually) exploited, leading to unsafe and unstable working environments and high teenage pregnancy rates.
